page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 3.9 GHz, it utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 2 threads per core under a burstable CPU allocation model. The compute subsystem is paired with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes extensive instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), and cryptographic primitives.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional compute and parallel processing throughput. The instance lands in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core performance (20,959.0), Clang compilation (58,924.0), and image processing (21,246.0), alongside top-tier static web serving throughput reaching 104.85 GB/sec. Stress-ng multi-core CPU testing registered 69,316.48, and PassMark CPU overall reached 83,206.18, both falling in the top 25%. Decompression and compression metrics are equally robust, marked by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 436.31 GB/sec. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 196.96 GB/sec, while cached read bandwidth reaches 5,116.7 GB/sec.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage via its 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Machine learning inference tasks on CPU benefit from AMX and AVX-512 extensions, yielding 303.91 tokens/sec on medium 7B model prompt processing (top 10%) and 3,350.53 tokens/sec on small 135M model prompts. However, text generation performance scales down with model size, averaging 3.53 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

The hardware configuration provides high compute density and cost efficiency for processing-heavy workloads that do not demand extensive per-core RAM. Tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe storage, burstable CPU scheduling limits, and average memory write throughput of 82.79 GB/sec. It is functionally targeted at large-scale software compilation, batch processing, static web serving infrastructure, Redis caching clusters, and CPU-based deep learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores at 3.9 GHz) powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor on the Nitro hypervisor. It is provisioned with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 15 Gbps baseline network capacity. The platform excludes dedicated local storage and GPUs, instead leveraging CPU vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in Clang code compilation (58,924.0), multi-core processing (Geekbench 20,959.0), and static web serving (104.85 GB/sec). Memory read bandwidth hits 196.96 GB/sec uncached, though write speeds remain average at 82.79 GB/sec. This configuration offers high compute density suited for software build pipelines, distributed cache nodes, data compression routines, and CPU-driven model inference.
